scope: updated hashes and conclusions for next-30 batch after semantic corrections

reviews.evidence: The core selects a probability distribution from a feasible class; distribution-law is therefore a direct object concept, while entropy choices and moment constraints remain later alternatives.
The conclusion asserts uniqueness up to almost-everywhere equality, so that concept is direct; probability-specific applications remain later prose.
The core compares measures on one measurable space and uses an RN derivative under absolute continuity; measurable-space was added to the object boundary.

Outer measure is the input, while sigma-algebra and measure are named outputs whose definitions are needed to understand the conclusion; those two prerequisites are retained. The criterion itself is defined inline.
The core identity integrates nonnegative measurable functions against a pushforward; Lebesgue integral is direct, while integrable-function is only required by the later finite-valued variant.

The theorem requires two sigma-finite measure spaces, a measurable function, product measure, and absolute integrability; l1-function/product-measure/integral plus measurable-function capture those direct ingredients. Tonelli is only a comparison.

The core assumes a measurable integrable function on a probability measure space and a convex function; measurable-function was added alongside the existing convexity, integral, L1, and measure-space concepts.
The core is measurable and essentially bounded on a measure space, so measure-space, measurable-function, and essential-supremum suffice. Quotient/a.e. material is later.
The core defines integrable measurable functions modulo a.e. equality; lp-norm and lp-space are later equivalent descriptions and were removed from the prerequisite boundary.
The norm definition requires measure space, measurable function, nonnegative integration, absolute value, and essential supremum for p=infinity. A.e. quotient discussion is later and was removed.
The core is a function between measurable spaces whose preimages lie in the domain sigma-algebra; measurable-set is not an additional direct prerequisite and was removed.
The core forms a product of measurable sets in two measurable spaces; Cartesian product, measurable-space, and measurable-set are all direct ingredients.
